title: CS Wayfinder: consolidated intake sketch for prioritizing enterprise feature asks
creator: Asha Patel
description: Problem: Sales and Customer Success funnel a lot of enterprise feature asks (non-bug) via many channels: meetings, email, spreadsheets, and ad-hoc notes. That creates duplicate asks, inconsistent prioritization, and slow handoffs to PM/Eng. Goal: create a lightweight, repeatable "Wayfinder" intake sketch that aggregates incoming enterprise requests, surfaces duplicates and strategic fit, and outputs a small, scored batch for initial scoping within a single week. Scope: Sales/CS -> PM handoff for non-bug enterprise asks only. Excludes urgent incidents, legal/compliance requests (those route to Security/Legal), and device/on-prem infra projects which follow Dedicated intake flows.
acceptance_criteria:
1) A documented "Wayfinder" artifact (spreadsheet + decision rubric) that consolidates recent 6-week enterprise asks and groups them into themes.
2) Scoring rubric that includes Strategic Alignment, Customer Economic Value, Implementation Risk, and Time-to-value, with clear weighting.
3) A 1-week cadence process for CS/Sales to submit a short intake record and for PM to produce an "Initial 3" prioritized list with rough estimates and blockers.
4) Pilot with 3 accounts (AM-owned) and one partner sales motion completed with recorded feedback.
5) Links to at least one technical feasibility note from Eng and one cost/ops note from Infra for each of the Initial 3.
notes:
Design decisions: keep intake light (<= 6 fields) to maximize adoption; automated dedupe by canonical account + problem statement to reduce duplicates; use a semi-quantitative score (0-10) instead of binary gates to surface trade-offs. Trade-offs discussed in kickoff: fast vs. precise scoring (we favor speed for first-pass), and centralization vs. local autonomy (we'll allow account-level owners to flag special strategic bets). Potential risk: repeated manual effort if CS doesn't commit — mitigation: surface individual user usage metrics in console and tie pilot adoption to AE bonus conversation. Technical feasibility: ENG-1842 to provide a 30-minute feasibility template for common infra asks.
Follow-ups: refine scoring weights after pilot; prepare a short training doc for CS and Sales; integrate with Zendesk/Gong capture signals in next phase.
updates: 2026-03-02: Kickoff workshop with CS (Jared Morris), Sales Engineering (Priya Rao), and Eng scoping representative (Diego Morales). Agreed on 6-field intake: account, problem statement (1-2 sentences), business outcome, estimated ARR impact, desired timeline, and contact/owner.

2026-03-04: Built initial spreadsheet prototype and dedupe rules. CS provided a dataset of 42 asks from the last 8 weeks; dedupe reduced to 28 unique asks. Preliminary clustering identified 4 themes: observability, model selection routing, private deployment onboarding, and cost controls for embeddings.

2026-03-06: Scoring rubric drafted: Strategic Alignment (30%), Customer Econ (30%), Implementation Risk (20%), Time-to-value (20%). Discussed alternate weighting; product leadership prefers higher weight on Customer Econ for pilot.

2026-03-08: Quick eng feasibility checks for top 6 asks — two flagged as low-risk, one requires Dedicated infra changes (dependency ENG-1842), one needs KMS clarification (security consult requested), two need further product-scoped design. Assigned follow-ups to ENG and Security.
2026-03-10: Pilot cohort selected (Accounts: AtlasHealth, MeridianRetail, NovaFin). PMs to run 1-week scoping per account and report back by 2026-03-20. Liam to prepare CS training one-pager.
2026-03-10: Raised potential dependency on console routing metrics (ENG dashboard access) — reached out to Observability team to grant temporary access to PM and CS leads.
2026-03-10: Reviewed with Head of Sales (Maya Thompson) — she approved pilot and requested SLA for follow-up communication with requesting AE within 48 hours of intake submission.
